title: Source tax tariff: children
purpose: Ask employees subject to source tax whether they have children, then ask the calculator's questions once per child. Each child's answers decide whether that child counts toward the child digit, and whether it makes the tariff letter H for single employees. Before go-live, a domain expert checks the paths that were not observed in the calculator.

stories.title: Ask about children only of employees who need a source tax tariff
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask whether the employee has biological or adopted children, but only when the employee is subject to source tax
stories.so_that: the child digit of the tariff code can be worked out, and no data about children is collected from employees who do not need a tariff
stories.priority_reason: Without this answer Lonio cannot compute the tariff code (D-001). Today HR has to click through the calculator by hand. Asking everyone would collect personal data that no party needs (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: The children question is asked only of employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: The employee has answered the questions that decide whether they are subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax: country of residence and, for residents of Switzerland, Swiss citizenship, C permit, civil status and spouse details)
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: Employees subject to source tax are asked whether they have children and must answer it. This includes everyone living abroad, Liechtenstein residents among them. Employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: The question covers the spouse's or partner's children for married employees and registered partners
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax is asked whether they have children
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee's civil status is Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.then: The question asks about biological or adopted children of the employee or of the spouse / registered partner. For Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated employees it asks only about the employee's own biological or adopted children. The answer is "yes" or "no".

acceptance_criteria.title: No children: no child questions and child digit 0
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: No per-child questions are asked and the child digit of the tariff code is 0. When they answer "yes", the questions for the first child start.

stories.title: One block per child: age status and household
stories.i_want: to describe each of my children separately, starting with whether the child is a minor or an adult in first education and whether the child lives in my household
stories.so_that: each child is assessed on its own facts, and I am not asked further questions about a child who cannot count for the tariff
stories.priority_reason: Each child's answers feed the computed tariff code (D-001). These are the entry questions of every child block.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child questions are answered once per child
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has answered "yes" to having children
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in the children part
acceptance_criteria.then: They answer the child questions separately for each child. They can add another child and remove a child entered by mistake. Each child gets its own result (counts, counts with H, or does not count). The questionnaire sets no maximum number of children; whether more than 3 children are handled like the calculator is still to be verified (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: Age status of each child
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax who has children
acceptance_criteria.then: They must state whether the child is "Minor", "Adult in first education" or "Neither". With "Neither" no further questions are asked about that child, and the child does not count for the tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Same household is asked for minors and adults in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has described a child as "Minor" or "Adult in first education"
acceptance_criteria.then: They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether the child lives in their household. The answer is used for the source tax tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child answers that no longer apply are not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee has answered child questions and then changes an earlier answer, so that some child questions no longer apply (for example, they become not subject to source tax, answer "no" to having children, or change a child to "Neither")
acceptance_criteria.then: The answers to child questions that no longer apply are discarded. Until submission they are kept, so that going back and forth loses no input.

stories.title: Minor child living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: the calculator's custody, common-household, alternating-custody and main-contributor questions for a minor child living in the employee's household, asked only as far as the calculator asks them
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide whether the child counts, and whether it counts with H for single employees, exactly as the calculator would
stories.priority_reason: The child digit and the H tariff depend on these answers. Lonio owns the tariff result (D-001), so a wrong branch produces a wrong tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Custody of a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has a child who is a "Minor" and lives in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: They must state whether they have "Shared custody" or "Sole custody". With sole custody the child counts: for married employees and registered partners it simply counts, for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees it counts with H. No further questions are asked about that child. The custody question is not asked about minors living outside the household.

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared custody and a common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has a minor child in their household with "Shared custody"
acceptance_criteria.then: They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent. With "yes": for married employees and registered partners the child counts and no further question is asked. Single, divorced, separated or widowed employees are asked who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance ("Employee" or "Other parent"): with "Employee" the child counts with H, with "Other parent" it does not count.

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared custody without a common household: alternating custody
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has a minor child in their household with "Shared custody" and does not live in a common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.then: They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether there is alternating custody. With "no": for married employees and registered partners the child does not count, for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees it counts with H. No further question is asked about that child.

acceptance_criteria.title: Alternating custody: who contributes most to maintenance
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has a minor child in their household with "Shared custody", no common household with the other parent and alternating custody
acceptance_criteria.then: They must state who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance, "Employee" or "Other parent". With "Employee" the child counts: married employees and registered partners get a plain count, single, divorced, separated or widowed employees get a count with H. With "Other parent" the child does not count. The married + Employee and single + Other parent results were not observed in the calculator and must be checked before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.title: Minor child not living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: the calculator's custody, alternating-custody and main-contributor questions for a minor child living outside the employee's household, with the custody question worded by civil status group
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide whether such a child counts, and whether it counts with H for single employees, as the calculator would
stories.priority_reason: This case affects the child digit and the H tariff of the computed tariff code (D-001). Several results here are inferred and are part of the go-live check (D-009).

acceptance_criteria.title: Married employees and registered partners: shared custody
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax whose civil status is Married or Registered partnership has a "Minor" child who does not live in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether custody is shared. The parental care question is not asked. With "no" the child does not count and no further question is asked about it.

acceptance_criteria.title: Single, divorced, separated or widowed employees: parental care
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax whose civil status is Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated has a "Minor" child who does not live in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether they have parental care. The shared-custody question is not asked. With "no" the child does not count and no further question is asked about it.

acceptance_criteria.title: Custody or parental care: alternating custody
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has a minor child outside their household. Either they are married or in a registered partnership with shared custody, or they are single, divorced, separated or widowed with parental care
acceptance_criteria.then: They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether there is alternating custody. With "no" the child does not count and no further question is asked about it. This result was not observed in the calculator and must be checked before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: Alternating custody: who contributes most to maintenance
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has a minor child outside their household with shared custody or parental care and alternating custody
acceptance_criteria.then: They must state who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance, "Employee" or "Other parent". With "Other parent" the child does not count. This last result was not observed in the calculator (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.title: Adult child in first education
stories.i_want: the calculator's common-household, main-contributor and maintenance questions for an adult child in first education
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide whether the child counts, and whether it counts with H for single employees, as the calculator would
stories.priority_reason: This case affects the child digit and the H tariff of the computed tariff code (D-001). Several results are inferred and part of the go-live check (D-009).

acceptance_criteria.title: Adult child in the household: common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has a child who is an "Adult in first education" and lives in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent. No custody questions are asked. With "yes": for married employees and registered partners the child counts and no further question is asked. Single, divorced, separated or widowed employees are asked who makes the larger financial contribution ("Employee" or "Other parent"): with "Employee" the child counts with H, with "Other parent" it does not count. The single-group results were not observed in the calculator (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: Adult child in the household without a common household: more than 50% of maintenance
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has an adult child in first education in their household and does not live in a common household with the other parent
acceptance_criteria.then: They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether they pay more than 50% of the child's maintenance. With "yes": single, divorced, separated or widowed employees count the child with H, married employees and registered partners count it. With "no" the child does not count. Only the single "yes" result was observed in the calculator; the others must be checked before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: Adult child outside the household: more than 50% of maintenance
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has an adult child in first education who does not live in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: The common-household question is not asked. They must answer "yes" or "no" to whether they pay more than 50% of the child's maintenance. With "yes" the child counts, without H, whatever the civil status. With "no" it does not count.

stories.title: Child digit of the tariff code and go-live check of the child paths
stories.i_want: the child digit of the tariff code to be the number of children who count, with the child paths not observed in the calculator verified before go-live
stories.so_that: the tariff code Lonio computes matches the calculator, without HR clicking through the calculator by hand
stories.priority_reason: Lonio replaces HR's manual calculator step and owns the tariff result (D-001). D-009 makes the verification a go-live condition.

acceptance_criteria.title: The child digit counts every child that counts, with or without H
acceptance_criteria.given: An employee subject to source tax has answered the children questions
acceptance_criteria.then: The child digit is the number of children whose result is 'counts' or 'counts with H' (for example, three children who count give the digit 3, as in C3Y). It is 0 if the employee has no children or no child counts. For single, divorced, separated or widowed employees, a child that counts with H is what makes the tariff letter H (see the tariff letter rule).

acceptance_criteria.title: The child digit always reflects the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: The children answers have been recorded and are later changed (after submission only HR can change them)
acceptance_criteria.when: the tariff code is derived again
acceptance_criteria.then: The per-child results and the child digit are computed from the latest answers. No earlier result is kept as the valid one.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child paths not observed in the calculator are verified before go-live
acceptance_criteria.given: Some per-child results were inferred rather than observed in the calculator, and more than 3 children were never tested (see OQ-calculator-coverage, non-blocking)
acceptance_criteria.when: the computed tariff code is prepared for release
acceptance_criteria.then: Before go-live a domain expert has compared Lonio's per-child results and child digit with the calculator for every inferred child path and for more than 3 children, and any difference has been resolved. Special tariffs such as D (second job) are not part of this check.
